findings.evidence: `RegularityConditions.lean:98` uses `¬ AnalyticAt`; `ResidueTheorem.lean:21-25` says only negative meromorphic order matters and no pointwise regularity of raw `f` is required because isolated wrong values are ignored.
findings.fix: Drive the condition from the meromorphic/Laurent support, e.g. `meromorphicOrderAt f (γ t₀) < 0` or the higher-order principal-part support needed for condition (B), rather than raw `AnalyticAt`.
findings.issue: The interior clause triggers on `¬ AnalyticAt ℂ f (γ t₀)`, so a removable raw-value defect on the contour still forces `SectorCompatible`, including the rational-angle condition at line 85, even though the residue API is intentionally insensitive to isolated wrong values.

findings.evidence: `RegularityConditions.lean:102` uses `¬ AnalyticAt`; the roadmap theorem assumes meromorphicity at `S` (`Suggested.lean:220-226`) and the existing residue theorem normalizes away raw point values (`ResidueTheorem.lean:23-25`).
findings.fix: Use the same meromorphic-order/principal-part trigger as the interior clause for the basepoint case.
findings.issue: The same over-strong raw `¬ AnalyticAt` trigger is used at the basepoint, so removable endpoint value defects require sector compatibility despite carrying no pole or higher Laurent obstruction.

summary: `ConditionB` is stronger than the natural residue-theorem/Laurent level because it treats raw non-analytic point values as singularities needing angle compatibility.
